records.translation: Um arquivo de configurações executa um de dois níveis (``train_level``):

records.context: ``'well_set'``: the :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` on per-cell embeddings, scored by mechanism of action with its ablations and controls (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).
records.label: spacr.architecture_training#2
records.source: ``'well_set'``: the :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` on per-cell embeddings, scored by mechanism of action with its ablations and controls (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).
records.translation: ``'well_set'``: o :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` sobre embeddings por célula, pontuado por mecanismo de ação com as suas ablações e controles (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).

records.context: ``'cell'``: the image data channel-adaptive CNN or ViT (``train_arch``) on single-cell extracted image regions (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Optionally the ViT is first pre-trained without labels (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al. 2022, or ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) for ``pretrain_epochs`` epochs; ``train_labels_per_class`` then keeps only that many labelled cells per class (few-shot). Every model is scored on the full stain panel and on each subset of ``eval_channel_subsets`` (the missing-stain evaluation), beside a majority-class control and, with ``train_set_shuffle_control``, a model trained on shuffled labels.
records.label: spacr.architecture_training#3
records.source: ``'cell'``: the channel-adaptive CNN or ViT (``train_arch``) on single-cell crops (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Optionally the ViT is first pre-trained without labels (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al. 2022, or ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) for ``pretrain_epochs`` epochs; ``train_labels_per_class`` then keeps only that many labelled cells per class (few-shot). Every model is scored on the full stain panel and on each subset of ``eval_channel_subsets`` (the missing-stain evaluation), beside a majority-class control and, with ``train_set_shuffle_control``, a model trained on shuffled labels.
records.translation: ``'cell'``: a CNN ou ViT adaptativa aos canais (``train_arch``) sobre recortes de células individuais (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Opcionalmente, o ViT é primeiro pré-treinado sem rótulos (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al. 2022, ou ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) durante ``pretrain_epochs`` épocas; ``train_labels_per_class`` mantém então apenas esse número de células rotuladas por classe (few-shot). Cada modelo é pontuado no painel completo de marcadores e em cada subconjunto de ``eval_channel_subsets`` (a avaliação com marcadores ausentes), ao lado de um controle de classe majoritária e, com ``train_set_shuffle_control``, de um modelo treinado com rótulos embaralhados.

records.context: Cell extracted image regions come as one ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` array (``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) with a row-aligned table (``train_cell_table``) holding the label and the group (well) column; cells are split by group, so no well is in both training and test. The extracted image regions are raw: each image data channel is divided by the 99th percentile of up to 2,048 training extracted image regions, clipped at 1.5 and mapped by ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, the transform of the gene-class benchmark. Training augments by flips, 90-degree rotations and a per-image data channel gain within 10%.
records.label: spacr.architecture_training#4
records.source: Cell crops come as one ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` array (``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) with a row-aligned table (``train_cell_table``) holding the label and the group (well) column; cells are split by group, so no well is in both training and test. The crops are raw: each channel is divided by the 99th percentile of up to 2,048 training crops, clipped at 1.5 and mapped by ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, the transform of the gene-class benchmark. Training augments by flips, 90-degree rotations and a per-channel gain within 10%.
records.translation: Os recortes de células vêm como um único array ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` (``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) com uma tabela alinhada por linha (``train_cell_table``) que contém a coluna de rótulo e a de grupo (poço); as células são divididas por grupo, de modo que nenhum poço fica no treino e no teste ao mesmo tempo. Os recortes são brutos: cada canal é dividido pelo percentil 99 de até 2,048 recortes de treino, cortado em 1.5 e mapeado por ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, a transformação do benchmark de classes de genes. O treino aumenta os dados com espelhamentos, rotações de 90 graus e um ganho por canal dentro de 10%.

records.context: Image data channel-adaptive models for any stain panel: a CNN, a ViT and a microplate sample position set transformer.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#0
records.source: Channel-adaptive models for any stain panel: a CNN, a ViT and a well set transformer.
records.translation: Modelos adaptativos aos canais para qualquer painel de marcadores: uma CNN, um ViT e um transformer de conjuntos de poços.

records.context: All three models take any number of image data channels (1 to more than 10) with the same weights. Every image data channel is processed on its own and tagged with a learned stain embedding, looked up by stain name rather than by slot index, so BBBC021 "DNA" and an OPS "DAPI" share one vector and an unseen panel still runs.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#1
records.source: All three models take any number of channels (1 to more than 10) with the same weights. Every channel is processed on its own and tagged with a learned stain embedding, looked up by stain name rather than by slot index, so BBBC021 "DNA" and an OPS "DAPI" share one vector and an unseen panel still runs.
records.translation: Os três modelos aceitam qualquer número de canais (de 1 a mais de 10) com os mesmos pesos. Cada canal é processado isoladamente e marcado com um embedding de marcador aprendido, consultado pelo nome do marcador e não pelo índice da posição, de modo que "DNA" do BBBC021 e "DAPI" de um OPS partilham um vetor e um painel nunca visto ainda funciona.

records.context: :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` is an image data channel-adaptive ConvNeXt-style CNN: a HyperNet stem per image data channel, ConvNeXt blocks shared across image data channels and FiLM-conditioned on the stain, cross-image data channel attention at every spatial location (one feature map per image data channel is kept) and image data channel attention pooling at the end, which records the stain that drove the call.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#2
records.source: :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` is a channel-adaptive ConvNeXt-style CNN: a HyperNet stem per channel, ConvNeXt blocks shared across channels and FiLM-conditioned on the stain, cross-channel attention at every spatial location (one feature map per channel is kept) and channel attention pooling at the end, which records the stain that drove the call.
records.translation: :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` é uma CNN de estilo ConvNeXt adaptativa aos canais: um stem HyperNet por canal, blocos ConvNeXt partilhados entre canais e condicionados por FiLM ao marcador, atenção entre canais em cada posição espacial (mantém-se um mapa de variáveis por canal) e pooling de atenção sobre os canais no fim, que registra o marcador que determinou a decisão.

records.context: :class:`SpacrChannelViT` is an image data channel-aware ViT: per-image data channel patch tokens plus a stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position, an optional per-sample image data channel-availability mask for missing stains, and Hierarchical image data channel Sampling (image data channel dropout, Bao et al. 2024) in training. It is pre-trained with :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) or :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et al. 2021).
records.label: spacr.channel_models#3
records.source: :class:`SpacrChannelViT` is a channel-aware ViT: per-channel patch tokens plus a stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position, an optional per-sample channel-availability mask for missing stains, and Hierarchical Channel Sampling (channel dropout, Bao et al. 2024) in training. It is pre-trained with :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) or :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et al. 2021).
records.translation: :class:`SpacrChannelViT` é um ViT consciente dos canais: tokens de patch por canal mais um embedding de marcador e uma posição 2-D sin-cos, uma máscara opcional de disponibilidade de canais por amostra para marcadores ausentes, e Hierarchical Channel Sampling (dropout de canais, Bao et al. 2024) no treino. É pré-treinado com :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) ou :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et al. 2021).

records.context: :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` is a set model over the single-cell embeddings of a well. Mode ``'arrayed'``: an ISAB set encoder (Lee et al. 2019) and gated multi-head attention-MIL pooling (Ilse et al. 2018) give the well logits, the attention weights and per-cell instance logits (the penetrant fraction, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Mode ``'pooled'``: per-cell logits conditioned on a context set of other cells of the same well; an empty context is a learned null token, so the no-context ablation is the same model with set size 0.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#4
records.source: :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` is a set model over the single-cell embeddings of a well. Mode ``'arrayed'``: an ISAB set encoder (Lee et al. 2019) and gated multi-head attention-MIL pooling (Ilse et al. 2018) give the well logits, the attention weights and per-cell instance logits (the penetrant fraction, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Mode ``'pooled'``: per-cell logits conditioned on a context set of other cells of the same well; an empty context is a learned null token, so the no-context ablation is the same model with set size 0.
records.translation: :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` é um modelo de conjuntos sobre os embeddings de células individuais de um poço. Modo ``'arrayed'``: um codificador de conjuntos ISAB (Lee et al. 2019) e pooling attention-MIL multi-cabeça com comportas (Ilse et al. 2018) dão os logits do poço, os pesos de atenção e os logits de instância por célula (a fração penetrante, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Modo ``'pooled'``: logits por célula condicionados a um conjunto de contexto de outras células do mesmo poço; um contexto vazio é um token nulo aprendido, de modo que a ablação sem contexto é o mesmo modelo com tamanho de conjunto 0.

records.translation: :func:`build_channel_model` é o registro: constrói qualquer um dos três pelo nome em :data:`CHANNEL_ARCHITECTURES`, que é também o que a configuração de treino ``train_arch`` e :func:`spacr.utils.choose_model` aceitam. :class:`ChannelClassifier` dá aos dois modelos de imagem a interface ``model(x) -> logits`` do resto do caminho de treino do spaCR.

records.source: ``mask_ratio`` of all ``C * N`` tokens is masked at random, and with probability ``p_whole_channel`` per sample one whole channel is masked in addition, so the model learns to predict one stain from the others. One decoder is shared by all channels; the stain embedding tells it which to paint. The loss is the mean squared error on the masked patches, each patch normalised to zero mean and unit variance.
records.translation: ``mask_ratio`` de todos os ``C * N`` tokens é mascarado ao acaso e, com probabilidade ``p_whole_channel`` por amostra, um canal inteiro é mascarado adicionalmente, de modo que o modelo aprende a prever um marcador a partir dos outros. Um único decodificador é partilhado por todos os canais; o embedding do marcador diz-lhe qual pintar. A perda é o erro quadrático médio nos patches mascarados, cada patch normalizado para média zero e variância unitária.

records.translation: Tamanho padrão: dims (32, 64, 128, 256), depths (2, 2, 4, 2), cerca de 2.4 M parâmetros. Altura e largura devem ser divisíveis por 32 (96, 128 e 224 funcionam). records.context: Tokens: one shared one-image data channel patch embedding per image data channel, plus the stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position shared over image data channels, so ``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens and a CLS token. Default img 224 and patch 32 (49 tokens per image data channel). The native-resolution arm is img 96 / patch 12 (OPS) or img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). With ``bag_of_channels`` every image data channel is a separate sequence and the per-image data channel CLS vectors are fused late, which is cheaper and the better self-supervised setting on CHAMMI-75.
records.label: spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT#1
records.source: Tokens: one shared one-channel patch embedding per channel, plus the stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position shared over channels, so ``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens and a CLS token. Default img 224 and patch 32 (49 tokens per channel). The native-resolution arm is img 96 / patch 12 (OPS) or img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). With ``bag_of_channels`` every channel is a separate sequence and the per-channel CLS vectors are fused late, which is cheaper and the better self-supervised setting on CHAMMI-75.
records.translation: Tokens: um embedding de patch de um canal partilhado por canal, mais o embedding do marcador e uma posição 2-D sin-cos partilhada entre canais, portanto ``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens e um token CLS. Padrão img 224 e patch 32 (49 tokens por canal). O braço de resolução nativa é img 96 / patch 12 (OPS) ou img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). Com ``bag_of_channels``, cada canal é uma sequência separada e os vetores CLS por canal são fundidos no fim, o que é mais barato e a melhor configuração autossupervisionada no CHAMMI-75.

records.context: The nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 machine-learning classification models, built as CellProfiler Analyst builds them.
records.label: spacr.cpa_classifiers#0
records.source: The nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 classifiers, built as CellProfiler Analyst builds them.
records.translation: Os nove classificadores do CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5, construídos como o CellProfiler Analyst os constrói.

records.context: CellProfiler Analyst (CPA; github.com/CellProfiler/CellProfiler-Analyst, commit f5e1b5e2b2c35bb1aff4516ae5a49fe420df0350, version 3.0.5, BSD 3-Clause licence, Copyright 2003-2024 Broad Institute) offers nine machine-learning classification models in its machine-learning classification model window. Eight are scikit-learn estimators that CPA's ``GeneralClassifier`` constructs from a fixed string, with an optional :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fitted on the training data; :data:`CPA_GENERAL` holds the strings and scaler flags verbatim from ``cpa/classifier.py``. The ninth, FastGentleBoosting, is CPA's own boosted stumps (Torralba et al. 2007, "Sharing visual features for multiclass and multiview object detection", ieee pami), ported here from ``cpa/fastgentleboosting.py`` with the same arithmetic in ``float32``, the same unstable ``argsort`` and the same tie rule, and scored as CPA scores cells (sum over rules of ``a`` if ``x > threshold`` else ``b``, argmax).
records.label: spacr.cpa_classifiers#1
records.source: CellProfiler Analyst (CPA; github.com/CellProfiler/CellProfiler-Analyst, commit f5e1b5e2b2c35bb1aff4516ae5a49fe420df0350, version 3.0.5, BSD 3-Clause licence, Copyright 2003-2024 Broad Institute) offers nine classifiers in its Classifier window. Eight are scikit-learn estimators that CPA's ``GeneralClassifier`` constructs from a fixed string, with an optional :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fitted on the training data; :data:`CPA_GENERAL` holds the strings and scaler flags verbatim from ``cpa/classifier.py``. The ninth, FastGentleBoosting, is CPA's own boosted stumps (Torralba et al. 2007, "Sharing visual features for multiclass and multiview object detection", IEEE PAMI), ported here from ``cpa/fastgentleboosting.py`` with the same arithmetic in ``float32``, the same unstable ``argsort`` and the same tie rule, and scored as CPA scores cells (sum over rules of ``a`` if ``x > threshold`` else ``b``, argmax).
records.translation: O CellProfiler Analyst (CPA; github.com/CellProfiler/CellProfiler-Analyst, commit f5e1b5e2b2c35bb1aff4516ae5a49fe420df0350, versão 3.0.5, licença BSD 3-Clause, Copyright 2003-2024 Broad Institute) oferece nove classificadores na sua janela Classifier. Oito são estimadores do scikit-learn que o ``GeneralClassifier`` do CPA constrói a partir de uma string fixa, com um :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` opcional ajustado aos dados de treino; :data:`CPA_GENERAL` guarda as strings e os indicadores do scaler literalmente de ``cpa/classifier.py``. O nono, FastGentleBoosting, são os stumps com boosting do próprio CPA (Torralba et al. 2007, "Sharing visual features for multiclass and multiview object detection", IEEE PAMI), portado aqui de ``cpa/fastgentleboosting.py`` com a mesma aritmética em ``float32``, o mesmo ``argsort`` instável e a mesma regra de desempate, e pontuado como o CPA pontua células (soma sobre as regras de ``a`` se ``x > threshold``, senão ``b``, argmax).

records.context: :func:`make_cpa_model` returns an estimator with ``fit``, ``predict`` and ``predict_proba``; :func:`spacr.moa_benchmark.loco_supervised` fits it as ``cpa_<name>``, such as ``cpa_RandomForestClassifier``. A machine-learning classification model that takes a ``random_state`` gets the fold's seed, as the BBBC021 reanalysis (``cpa_models.py``) set it. FastGentleBoosting has no probabilities: its additive scores go through a softmax so that averaging over a treatment's microplate sample positions is defined.

A classifier that takes a ``random_state`` gets the fold's seed, as the BBBC021 reanalysis (``cpa_models.py``) set it. records.context: The computer-vision arm of the BBBC021 benchmark, from settings, in four steps that :func:`run_embedding_profiles` runs in order:
records.label: spacr.embedding_profiles#1
records.source: The computer-vision arm of the BBBC021 benchmark, from settings, in four steps that :func:`run_embedding_profiles` runs in order:
records.translation: O braço de visão computacional do benchmark BBBC021, a partir das configurações, em quatro passos que :func:`run_embedding_profiles` executa em ordem:

records.context: 1. :func:`write_crop_shard` cuts a fixed-size window around each chosen cell of a laboratory microplate from its merged microscope fields of view (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`), raw: never stretched per extracted image region (item 772), optionally divided by the laboratory microplate's saved flat microscope field of view (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), with a bit-flag mask (1 this cell, 2 any nucleus, 4 another cell, 8 outside the microscope field of view). At most ``crop_cap_per_well`` cells per microplate sample position are drawn by ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, microplate sample position by microplate sample position in sorted order. One HDF5 shard per laboratory microplate holds ``images`` and ``masks``, beside a ``.cells.parquet`` with one row per extracted image region; 2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` encodes the masked extracted image regions with a pretrained backbone (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), each image data channel alone, under one fixed scale per laboratory microplate and image data channel (the 99th percentile of a 2,048-extracted image region sample, item 410); 3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` writes ``wells_median.parquet``, ``wells_mean.parquet`` and the control cells' percentiles in the layout of the feature aggregate (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`), so :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` scores them unchanged; 4. :func:`well_umap` writes a UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) of the microplate sample positions.
records.label: spacr.embedding_profiles#2
records.source: 1. :func:`write_crop_shard` cuts a fixed-size window around each chosen cell of a plate from its merged fields (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`), raw: never stretched per crop (item 772), optionally divided by the plate's saved flat field (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), with a bit-flag mask (1 this cell, 2 any nucleus, 4 another cell, 8 outside the field). At most ``crop_cap_per_well`` cells per well are drawn by ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, well by well in sorted order. One HDF5 shard per plate holds ``images`` and ``masks``, beside a ``.cells.parquet`` with one row per crop; 2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` encodes the masked crops with a pretrained backbone (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), each channel alone, under one fixed scale per plate and channel (the 99th percentile of a 2,048-crop sample, item 410); 3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` writes ``wells_median.parquet``, ``wells_mean.parquet`` and the control cells' percentiles in the layout of the feature aggregate (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`), so :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` scores them unchanged; 4. :func:`well_umap` writes a UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) of the wells.
records.translation: 1. :func:`write_crop_shard` corta uma janela de tamanho fixo em torno de cada célula escolhida de uma placa a partir dos seus campos mesclados (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`), em bruto: nunca esticada por recorte (item 772), opcionalmente dividida pelo campo plano salvo da placa (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), com uma máscara de bits (1 esta célula, 2 qualquer núcleo, 4 outra célula, 8 fora do campo). No máximo ``crop_cap_per_well`` células por poço são sorteadas por ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, poço a poço em ordem. Um fragmento HDF5 por placa guarda ``images`` e ``masks``, ao lado de um ``.cells.parquet`` com uma linha por recorte; 2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` codifica os recortes mascarados com um backbone pré-treinado (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), cada canal isoladamente, sob uma escala fixa por placa e canal (o percentil 99 de uma amostra de 2,048 recortes, item 410); 3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` grava ``wells_median.parquet``, ``wells_mean.parquet`` e os percentis das células de controle no layout da agregação de variáveis (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`), de modo que :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` os pontua sem alterações; 4. :func:`well_umap` grava um UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) dos poços.

records.context: For each cell the window of side ``size`` centred on its rounded centroid in the ``cell`` label image layer is read from ``merged/<plate>_<well>_<site>_1.npy`` (zero padded past the edge). With ``illumination`` the laboratory microplate's flat field is applied as Measure applies it: ``rint((window - offset) * gain)``, clipped to uint16 and the clipped pixels counted. ``mask_flags`` adds the bit mask of :data:`MASK_BITS`. Writes ``<out>/<plate>.h5`` (``images`` uint16 ``(n, size, size, channels)`` and ``masks`` uint8, gzip 4, chunks of 32), ``<plate>.cells.parquet`` (the cells in shard order with ``row``, centroid, bounding box, mask area, clipped pixels and ``truncated``) and ``<plate>.json``.
records.label: spacr.embedding_profiles.write_crop_shard#1
records.source: For each cell the window of side ``size`` centred on its rounded centroid in the ``cell`` label plane is read from ``merged/<plate>_<well>_<site>_1.npy`` (zero padded past the edge). With ``illumination`` the plate's flat field is applied as Measure applies it: ``rint((window - offset) * gain)``, clipped to uint16 and the clipped pixels counted. ``mask_flags`` adds the bit mask of :data:`MASK_BITS`. Writes ``<out>/<plate>.h5`` (``images`` uint16 ``(n, size, size, channels)`` and ``masks`` uint8, gzip 4, chunks of 32), ``<plate>.cells.parquet`` (the cells in shard order with ``row``, centroid, bounding box, mask area, clipped pixels and ``truncated``) and ``<plate>.json``.
records.translation: Para cada célula, a janela de lado ``size`` centrada no seu centroide arredondado no plano de rótulos ``cell`` é lida de ``merged/<plate>_<well>_<site>_1.npy`` (preenchida com zeros além da borda). Com ``illumination``, o campo plano da placa é aplicado como Measure o aplica: ``rint((window - offset) * gain)``, cortado para uint16 e com os pixels cortados contados. ``mask_flags`` adiciona a máscara de bits de :data:`MASK_BITS`. Grava ``<out>/<plate>.h5`` (``images`` uint16 ``(n, size, size, channels)`` e ``masks`` uint8, gzip 4, blocos de 32), ``<plate>.cells.parquet`` (as células na ordem do fragmento com ``row``, centroide, caixa delimitadora, área da máscara, pixels cortados e ``truncated``) e ``<plate>.json``.

records.context: 1. the extracted image regions: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, a ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16 ``.npy`` with an index table holding ``scale0..`` per cell) or :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, cell-masked TIFF extracted image regions in tar shards with ``.index.csv`` byte offsets and a per-laboratory microplate scale file). Both divide by a fixed per-laboratory microplate, per-image data channel scale and clip, so extracted image regions stay raw on disk; 2. the labels and folds: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (MoA classes and the NSCB / NSC folds of :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) or :func:`ops_fold_setup` (multi-label gene classes from the :mod:`spacr.gene_classes` tables, gene folds, decoy heads, the shuffled control and the per-gene loss weight); 3. the sampler (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`, class-uniform for BBBC021 and, for OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (half the batch from positive genes, class then gene then cell; half from negative genes); 4. the model (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`): :func:`build_image_model` with the first convolution adapted to the image data channel count (:func:`adapt_first_conv`); 5. the transform: :func:`transform_spec` records the whole preprocessing, which is saved with the fold and checked again before scoring (:func:`check_transform`, item 772). :class:`DevicePrep` applies it on the device, with the train-time augmentation (dihedral, shift of up to 4 px, per-image data channel gain 0.9 to 1.1); 6. :func:`train_image_fold` trains with AdamW and a cosine schedule (AMP on a GPU, micro-batch halving on out-of-memory) and scores the held-out cells; :func:`score_bbbc_run` scores a BBBC021 run per microplate sample position and per treatment.
records.label: spacr.gene_class_images#2
records.source: 1. the crops: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, a ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16 ``.npy`` with an index table holding ``scale0..`` per cell) or :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, cell-masked TIFF crops in tar shards with ``.index.csv`` byte offsets and a per-plate scale file). Both divide by a fixed per-plate, per-channel scale and clip, so crops stay raw on disk; 2. the labels and folds: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (MoA classes and the NSCB / NSC folds of :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) or :func:`ops_fold_setup` (multi-label gene classes from the :mod:`spacr.gene_classes` tables, gene folds, decoy heads, the shuffled control and the per-gene loss weight); 3. the sampler (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`, class-uniform for BBBC021 and, for OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (half the batch from positive genes, class then gene then cell; half from negative genes); 4. the model (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`): :func:`build_image_model` with the first convolution adapted to the channel count (:func:`adapt_first_conv`); 5. the transform: :func:`transform_spec` records the whole preprocessing, which is saved with the fold and checked again before scoring (:func:`check_transform`, item 772). :class:`DevicePrep` applies it on the device, with the train-time augmentation (dihedral, shift of up to 4 px, per-channel gain 0.9 to 1.1); 6. :func:`train_image_fold` trains with AdamW and a cosine schedule (AMP on a GPU, micro-batch halving on out-of-memory) and scores the held-out cells; :func:`score_bbbc_run` scores a BBBC021 run per well and per treatment.
records.translation: 1. os recortes: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, um array ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16 em ``.npy`` com uma tabela de índice que guarda ``scale0..`` por célula) ou :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, recortes TIFF mascarados à célula em fragmentos tar com deslocamentos em bytes em ``.index.csv`` e um arquivo de escalas por placa). Ambos dividem por uma escala fixa por placa e por canal e cortam, de modo que os recortes permanecem brutos no disco; 2. os rótulos e as partições: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (classes de MoA e as partições NSCB / NSC de :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) ou :func:`ops_fold_setup` (classes de genes multirrótulo das tabelas de :mod:`spacr.gene_classes`, partições por gene, cabeças isca, o controle embaralhado e o peso de perda por gene); 3. o amostrador (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`, uniforme por classe para o BBBC021 e, para OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (metade do lote de genes positivos, classe, depois gene, depois célula; metade de genes negativos); 4. o modelo (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`): :func:`build_image_model` com a primeira convolução adaptada ao número de canais (:func:`adapt_first_conv`); 5. a transformação: :func:`transform_spec` registra todo o pré-processamento, que é salvo com a partição e verificado de novo antes da pontuação (:func:`check_transform`, item 772). :class:`DevicePrep` aplica-o no dispositivo, com o aumento de dados do treino (diedral, deslocamento de até 4 px, ganho por canal de 0.9 a 1.1); 6. :func:`train_image_fold` treina com AdamW e um agendamento cosseno (AMP numa GPU, redução à metade do micro-lote em falta de memória) e pontua as células retidas; :func:`score_bbbc_run` pontua uma execução do BBBC021 por poço e por tratamento.

records.context: Gene classes of a pooled screening experiment, gene-grouped folds and the class-prediction benchmark.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes#0
records.source: Gene classes of a pooled screen, gene-grouped folds and the class-prediction benchmark.
records.translation: Classes de genes de um rastreio agrupado, partições agrupadas por gene e o benchmark de previsão de classes.

records.context: A gene class is a set of screened genes that share an annotation: a kinase group, family or subfamily (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway, a GO-slim biological process, or a direction of one of Funk et al. 2022's per-gene feature scores. :func:`build_gene_classes` builds the class table from versioned source files (md5 recorded), merges or drops near-duplicate classes, and splits the genes into folds with multi-label iterative stratification (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`), so every class has members in every fold and no gene is in two folds.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes#1
records.source: A gene class is a set of screened genes that share an annotation: a kinase group, family or subfamily (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway, a GO-slim biological process, or a direction of one of Funk et al. 2022's per-gene feature scores. :func:`build_gene_classes` builds the class table from versioned source files (md5 recorded), merges or drops near-duplicate classes, and splits the genes into folds with multi-label iterative stratification (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`), so every class has members in every fold and no gene is in two folds.
records.translation: Uma classe de genes é um conjunto de genes rastreados que partilham uma anotação: um grupo, família ou subfamília de quinases (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), um complexo CORUM, uma via KEGG, um processo biológico GO-slim ou uma direção de uma das pontuações de variáveis por gene de Funk et al. 2022. :func:`build_gene_classes` constrói a tabela de classes a partir de arquivos de origem versionados (com md5 registrado), mescla ou descarta classes quase duplicadas e divide os genes em partições com estratificação iterativa multirrótulo (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`), de modo que cada classe tem membros em todas as partições e nenhum gene está em duas partições.

records.context: :func:`train_gene_class_baseline` fits one logistic regression per class on a gene-level feature table, fold by fold, with optional decoy heads (random gene sets of the classes' sizes, the null of the discovery calls) and a shuffled-class control. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` scores the out-of-fold predictions: per-class AUROC and average precision with bootstrap intervals, specificity against phenotype-positive and overlapping-class non-members, and the two discovery lists (known members with a new image phenotype; predicted new functions) at BH q < 0.05 against the decoy heads.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes#2
records.source: :func:`train_gene_class_baseline` fits one logistic regression per class on a gene-level feature table, fold by fold, with optional decoy heads (random gene sets of the classes' sizes, the null of the discovery calls) and a shuffled-class control. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` scores the out-of-fold predictions: per-class AUROC and average precision with bootstrap intervals, specificity against phenotype-positive and overlapping-class non-members, and the two discovery lists (known members with a new image phenotype; predicted new functions) at BH q < 0.05 against the decoy heads.
records.translation: :func:`train_gene_class_baseline` ajusta uma regressão logística por classe sobre uma tabela de variáveis por gene, partição a partição, com cabeças isca opcionais (conjuntos aleatórios de genes com os tamanhos das classes, a hipótese nula das descobertas) e um controle de classes embaralhadas. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` pontua as previsões fora da partição: AUROC e precisão média por classe com intervalos bootstrap, especificidade frente a não membros com fenótipo positivo e de classes sobrepostas, e as duas listas de descobertas (membros conhecidos com um novo fenótipo de imagem; novas funções previstas) com BH q < 0.05 frente às cabeças isca.

records.context: Every annotated screened gene is a member of its class; the trainable members are all of them, or with ``gene_class_gating`` only those with a screening experiment phenotype. A class is kept with ``gene_class_min_train`` or more trainable members and at most ``gene_class_max_members`` members (a CORUM complex needs five members). Classes are then visited by source priority (kinase, CORUM, KEGG, GO-slim, Funk) and size; one whose members (or trainable members, without ``gene_class_merge``) overlap a kept class by ``gene_class_merge_jaccard`` is merged into it or dropped.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes.build_gene_classes#1
records.source: Every annotated screened gene is a member of its class; the trainable members are all of them, or with ``gene_class_gating`` only those with a screen phenotype. A class is kept with ``gene_class_min_train`` or more trainable members and at most ``gene_class_max_members`` members (a CORUM complex needs five members). Classes are then visited by source priority (kinase, CORUM, KEGG, GO-slim, Funk) and size; one whose members (or trainable members, without ``gene_class_merge``) overlap a kept class by ``gene_class_merge_jaccard`` is merged into it or dropped.

records.label: spacr.gene_classes.evaluate_gene_class_run#0
records.source: Score a gene-class run out of fold: per class, specificity, discovery and a summary.
records.translation: Pontua uma execução de classes de genes fora da partição: por classe, especificidade, descoberta e um resumo.

records.context: Per class (and decoy head) the positives are the held-out trainable members and the negatives every scored non-member; AUROC and AP with bootstrap intervals, AUROC against control pseudo-genes, against phenotype-positive non-members and against members of overlapping classes, for members unique to the class, and for members with and without a screening experiment phenotype. A class is specific when its AUROC interval is above 0.5 and both specificity AUROCs are above 0.5. Discovery: each head is z-scored over genes; with 100 or more size-matched decoy heads a gene's p value is its rank on the decoy heads (the gene-wise null), else against the pooled decoy z; BH within each type: (a) members without a screening experiment phenotype that score as members (a new image phenotype), (b) non-members of a specific class whose best class it is (a predicted new function).
records.label: spacr.gene_classes.evaluate_gene_class_run#1
records.source: Per class (and decoy head) the positives are the held-out trainable members and the negatives every scored non-member; AUROC and AP with bootstrap intervals, AUROC against control pseudo-genes, against phenotype-positive non-members and against members of overlapping classes, for members unique to the class, and for members with and without a screen phenotype. A class is specific when its AUROC interval is above 0.5 and both specificity AUROCs are above 0.5. Discovery: each head is z-scored over genes; with 100 or more size-matched decoy heads a gene's p value is its rank on the decoy heads (the gene-wise null), else against the pooled decoy z; BH within each type: (a) members without a screen phenotype that score as members (a new image phenotype), (b) non-members of a specific class whose best class it is (a predicted new function).
records.translation: Por classe (e por cabeça isca), os positivos são os membros treináveis retidos e os negativos todos os não membros pontuados; AUROC e AP com intervalos bootstrap, AUROC frente a pseudogenes de controle, frente a não membros com fenótipo positivo e frente a membros de classes sobrepostas, para membros exclusivos da classe e para membros com e sem fenótipo no rastreio. Uma classe é específica quando o seu intervalo de AUROC está acima de 0.5 e ambos os AUROC de especificidade estão acima de 0.5. Descoberta: cada cabeça é convertida em z sobre os genes; com 100 ou mais cabeças isca de tamanho correspondente, o valor p de um gene é a sua posição nas cabeças isca (a hipótese nula por gene), caso contrário frente ao z agregado das iscas; BH dentro de cada tipo: (a) membros sem fenótipo no rastreio que pontuam como membros (um novo fenótipo de imagem), (b) não membros de uma classe específica que é a sua melhor classe (uma nova função prevista).

records.context: Per fold the features are standardised on the training genes; for every class an L2 logistic regression (C = 1, balanced class weights) is fitted on its trainable members against the non-members (members that do not train are left out) and scores the held-out genes. A class with fewer than two training positives in a fold is not scored there.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes.train_gene_class_baseline#1
records.source: Per fold the features are standardised on the training genes; for every class an L2 logistic regression (C = 1, balanced class weights) is fitted on its trainable members against the non-members (members that do not train are left out) and scores the held-out genes. A class with fewer than two training positives in a fold is not scored there.
records.translation: Em cada partição, as variáveis são padronizadas nos genes de treino; para cada classe, uma regressão logística L2 (C = 1, pesos de classe balanceados) é ajustada nos seus membros treináveis contra os não membros (os membros que não treinam ficam de fora) e pontua os genes retidos. Uma classe com menos de dois positivos de treino numa partição não é pontuada nela.

records.context: Learn gene-gene links and gene-to-category membership from screening experiment gene profiles.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#0
records.source: Learn gene-gene links and gene-to-category membership from screen gene profiles.
records.translation: Aprende ligações gene-gene e a pertença de genes a categorias a partir dos perfis de genes do rastreio.

records.context: An optical pooled screening experiment gives one profile per gene. Whether those profiles say something about gene function that the published interaction maps did not already know is judged here by two protocols, each with its controls:
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#1
records.source: An optical pooled screen gives one profile per gene. Whether those profiles say something about gene function that the published interaction maps did not already know is judged here by two protocols, each with its controls:
records.translation: Um rastreio óptico agrupado dá um perfil por gene. Se esses perfis dizem algo sobre a função dos genes que os mapas de interação publicados ainda não sabiam é avaliado aqui por dois protocolos, cada um com os seus controles:

records.context: the **time split**: the model is trained on the gene-gene edges known in 2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) and scored on the edges added since (``gene_graph_new_edges``), among every gene pair that was not a 2022 edge;
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#2
records.source: the **time split**: the model is trained on the gene-gene edges known in 2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) and scored on the edges added since (``gene_graph_new_edges``), among every gene pair that was not a 2022 edge;
records.translation: a **divisão temporal**: o modelo é treinado nas arestas gene-gene conhecidas em 2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) e pontuado nas arestas adicionadas desde então (``gene_graph_new_edges``), entre todos os pares de genes que não eram arestas em 2022;

records.context: **held-out genes**: for fold ``k`` every edge and every category membership of the fold's genes is hidden; the model scores those genes against every gene and every category.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#3
records.source: **held-out genes**: for fold ``k`` every edge and every category membership of the fold's genes is hidden; the model scores those genes against every gene and every category.
records.translation: **genes retidos**: para a partição ``k``, todas as arestas e todas as pertenças a categorias dos genes da partição são ocultadas; o modelo pontua esses genes contra todos os genes e todas as categorias.

records.context: The steps, each callable on its own and all four in order by :func:`run_gene_graph` (what ``spacr-run gene_graph`` calls):
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#4
records.source: The steps, each callable on its own and all four in order by :func:`run_gene_graph` (what ``spacr-run gene_graph`` calls):
records.translation: Os passos, cada um executável isoladamente e os quatro em ordem por :func:`run_gene_graph` (o que ``spacr-run gene_graph`` chama):

records.context: :func:`build_gene_graph` assembles the nodes (screening experiment genes and non-targeting pseudo-genes), the feature blocks with their missing indicators, the typed edges, the categories and the folds;
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#5
records.source: :func:`build_gene_graph` assembles the nodes (screen genes and non-targeting pseudo-genes), the feature blocks with their missing indicators, the typed edges, the categories and the folds;
records.translation: :func:`build_gene_graph` monta os nós (genes do rastreio e pseudogenes não direcionados), os blocos de variáveis com os seus indicadores de ausência, as arestas tipadas, as categorias e as partições;

records.context: :func:`train_gene_graph` runs the models: a graph transformer (``gps``), GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), Hadamard logistic regression (``lr``) and a Laplacian-eigenmap embedding (``spectral``), plus the training-free baselines ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` and ``prior``, each over feature arms and under the controls ``shufX`` (features permuted among genes), ``shufY`` (labels relabelled by a gene permutation) and ``rewire`` (degree-preserving swaps);
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#6
records.source: :func:`train_gene_graph` runs the models: a graph transformer (``gps``), GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), Hadamard logistic regression (``lr``) and a Laplacian-eigenmap embedding (``spectral``), plus the training-free baselines ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` and ``prior``, each over feature arms and under the controls ``shufX`` (features permuted among genes), ``shufY`` (labels relabelled by a gene permutation) and ``rewire`` (degree-preserving swaps);
records.translation: :func:`train_gene_graph` executa os modelos: um transformer de grafos (``gps``), GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), regressão logística de Hadamard (``lr``) e um embedding por mapa de autovetores do Laplaciano (``spectral``), mais as linhas de base sem treino ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` e ``prior``, cada um sobre braços de variáveis e sob os controles ``shufX`` (variáveis permutadas entre genes), ``shufY`` (rótulos reatribuídos por uma permutação de genes) e ``rewire`` (trocas que preservam o grau);

records.context: :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` writes the time-split and held-out metrics, the per-fold summaries, the ablation table and the paired fold deltas;
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#7
records.source: :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` writes the time-split and held-out metrics, the per-fold summaries, the ablation table and the paired fold deltas;
records.translation: :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` grava as métricas da divisão temporal e dos genes retidos, os resumos por partição, a tabela de ablações e as diferenças pareadas por partição;

records.context: :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibrates the out-of-fold scores, controls the false discovery rate with the non-targeting pseudo-genes as decoys and writes the explained prediction lists.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#8
records.source: :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibrates the out-of-fold scores, controls the false discovery rate with the non-targeting pseudo-genes as decoys and writes the explained prediction lists.
records.translation: :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibra as pontuações fora da partição, controla a taxa de falsas descobertas com os pseudogenes não direcionados como iscas e grava as listas de previsões explicadas.

records.context: The models are plain PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn. They run on the device named by ``gene_graph_device``; a CUDA device that is not available falls back to the CPU. On CUDA, the card rule of the shared workstation applies: a processing session waits until the card total plus its cap stays below ``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` for ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` seconds, yields (saving a resume file) when the card goes over the limit, and stops when ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` GPU hours are used. On the CPU the computation is deterministic, so a rerun from the saved settings file writes the same tables.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#9
records.source: The models are plain PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn. They run on the device named by ``gene_graph_device``; a CUDA device that is not available falls back to the CPU. On CUDA, the card rule of the shared workstation applies: a run waits until the card total plus its cap stays below ``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` for ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` seconds, yields (saving a resume file) when the card goes over the limit, and stops when ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` GPU hours are used. On the CPU the computation is deterministic, so a rerun from the saved settings file writes the same tables.
records.translation: Os modelos são PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy e scikit-learn simples. São executados no dispositivo nomeado por ``gene_graph_device``; um dispositivo CUDA indisponível recorre à CPU. Em CUDA aplica-se a regra da placa gráfica da estação de trabalho partilhada: uma execução espera até que o total da placa mais o seu limite fique abaixo de ``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` durante ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` segundos, cede a placa (salvando um arquivo de retomada) quando a placa ultrapassa o limite e para quando ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` horas de GPU forem usadas. Na CPU o cálculo é determinístico, de modo que uma nova execução a partir do arquivo de configurações salvo grava as mesmas tabelas.

records.context: Per epoch (graph models), ``node_mask`` of the supervisable genes are node-masked (held-out tasks) and ``edge_mask`` of the other training edges are hidden and supervised; negatives are ``neg_per_pos`` per positive, half uniform and half degree-proportional, never a known pair. ``lr`` supervises every training edge (a minibatch of positives) and every training gene. Early stopping on the inner validation keeps the best state. The final scoring graph holds every training edge with the validation genes restored; test genes stay isolated. Every epoch draws from ``default_rng([seed, s, epoch])`` and the resume file carries the torch random state, so a resumed run scores like an uninterrupted one.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph.run_config#1
records.source: Per epoch (graph models), ``node_mask`` of the supervisable genes are node-masked (held-out tasks) and ``edge_mask`` of the other training edges are hidden and supervised; negatives are ``neg_per_pos`` per positive, half uniform and half degree-proportional, never a known pair. ``lr`` supervises every training edge (a minibatch of positives) and every training gene. Early stopping on the inner validation keeps the best state. The final scoring graph holds every training edge with the validation genes restored; test genes stay isolated. Every epoch draws from ``default_rng([seed, s, epoch])`` and the resume file carries the torch random state, so a resumed run scores like an uninterrupted one.
records.translation: Em cada época (modelos de grafo), ``node_mask`` dos genes supervisionáveis são mascarados como nós (tarefas de genes retidos) e ``edge_mask`` das outras arestas de treino são ocultadas e supervisionadas; os negativos são ``neg_per_pos`` por positivo, metade uniformes e metade proporcionais ao grau, nunca um par conhecido. ``lr`` supervisiona todas as arestas de treino (um minilote de positivos) e todos os genes de treino. A parada antecipada na validação interna mantém o melhor estado. O grafo final de pontuação contém todas as arestas de treino com os genes de validação restaurados; os genes de teste permanecem isolados. Cada época sorteia de ``default_rng([seed, s, epoch])`` e o arquivo de retomada guarda o estado aleatório do torch, de modo que uma execução retomada pontua como uma ininterrupta.

records.context: What a screen adds to gene-function prediction can only be stated against what prior protein knowledge alone predicts. This module builds that knowledge on the gene graph's node order (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): one row per screen gene and one per non-targeting pseudo-gene.
records.label: spacr.gene_knowledge#1
records.source: What a screen adds to gene-function prediction can only be stated against what prior protein knowledge alone predicts. This module builds that knowledge on the gene graph's node order (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): one row per screen gene and one per non-targeting pseudo-gene.
records.translation: O que um rastreio acrescenta à previsão da função de genes só pode ser afirmado frente ao que o conhecimento prévio sobre proteínas prevê por si só. Este módulo constrói esse conhecimento na ordem dos nós do grafo de genes (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): uma linha por gene do rastreio e uma por pseudogene não direcionado.

records.context: No hosted model or API is used. Models run from local Hugging Face weights (``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); they are downloaded only when ``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` is on. Every step can instead reuse the stored output of an earlier run (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``, ``foldseek_alignments``), which is how a processing session is repeated without a GPU.
records.label: spacr.gene_knowledge#10
records.source: No hosted model or API is used. Models run from local Hugging Face weights (``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); they are downloaded only when ``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` is on. Every step can instead reuse the stored output of an earlier run (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``, ``foldseek_alignments``), which is how a run is repeated without a GPU.
records.translation: Não é usado nenhum modelo hospedado nem API. Os modelos são executados a partir de pesos locais do Hugging Face (``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); só são transferidos quando ``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` está ativado. Em vez disso, cada passo pode reutilizar a saída armazenada de uma execução anterior (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``, ``foldseek_alignments``), que é como uma execução é repetida sem GPU.

records.label: spacr.gene_knowledge#2
records.source: :func:`fetch_protein_annotations`: UniProt sequences, Pfam / InterPro cross-references and function text, current (REST, batches of at most 100 accessions) and from an archived Swiss-Prot release (``.dat`` streamed out of the release tarball); plus a seeded draw of reviewed human proteins outside the library, the decoys' knowledge;
records.translation: :func:`fetch_protein_annotations`: sequências UniProt, referências cruzadas Pfam / InterPro e texto de função, atuais (REST, lotes de no máximo 100 acessos) e de uma versão arquivada do Swiss-Prot (``.dat`` lido em fluxo a partir do tarball da versão); mais um sorteio com semente de proteínas humanas revisadas fora da biblioteca, o conhecimento das iscas;

records.source: Reads the merged arrays of ``translocation_merged_folder`` (or ``<src>/merged``). With ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` above 0 a five-plane array ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` gets its cell plane from the nuclei first (:func:`nucleus_territories`) and becomes the six-plane layout; a six-plane array already has its cell plane (Make Masks grows the territories itself with the same setting) and is read as it is. Cells are marked ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory when the territories were grown here or the merged folder's plane layout says Make Masks grew them; the territories are not cell outlines. Then :func:`translocation_cells` per field and :func:`translocation_summary`, written to ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, the summary tables, reference_curve.csv when ``translocation_reference`` names a reference curve table, and the translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles figure of :func:`translocation_figure`).
records.translation: Lê os arrays mesclados de ``translocation_merged_folder`` (ou ``<src>/merged``). Com ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` acima de 0, um array de cinco planos ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` recebe primeiro o seu plano de células a partir dos núcleos (:func:`nucleus_territories`) e passa ao layout de seis planos; um array de seis planos já tem o seu plano de células (Make Masks expande os territórios ele próprio com a mesma configuração) e é lido tal como está. As células são marcadas ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory quando os territórios foram expandidos aqui ou quando o layout de planos da pasta mesclada indica que Make Masks os expandiu; os territórios não são contornos de células. records.label: spacr.host_pathogen.write_nucleus_territories#1
records.source: For every field in ``<mask_src>/nucleus_mask_stack`` the nuclei under ``min_nucleus_size`` pixels are removed and the rest grow by up to ``expand_px`` pixels (:func:`nucleus_territories`). The territories are written to ``<mask_src>/cell_mask_stack`` and the kept nuclei to ``<mask_src>/nucleus_territory_seed_stack``, both as ``.npy`` in the nucleus mask's dtype, so the merged arrays carry a cell plane, the nucleus plane holds the nuclei the territories grew from, and Measure reads them like any other cell mask.
records.translation: Para cada campo em ``<mask_src>/nucleus_mask_stack``, os núcleos com menos de ``min_nucleus_size`` pixels são removidos e os restantes expandem-se até ``expand_px`` pixels (:func:`nucleus_territories`). Os territórios são gravados em ``<mask_src>/cell_mask_stack`` e os núcleos mantidos em ``<mask_src>/nucleus_territory_seed_stack``, ambos como ``.npy`` no dtype da máscara de núcleos, de modo que os arrays mesclados têm um plano de células, o plano de núcleos contém os núcleos a partir dos quais os territórios se expandiram, e Measure lê-os como qualquer outra máscara de células.

records.translation: ``'logistic'`` padroniza as variáveis na partição de treino e ajusta uma regressão logística multinomial L2 (C = 1). ``'xgboost'`` ajusta o XGBoost com :data:`XGBOOST_PARAMS` na CPU (:func:`spacr.ml._xgboost_cpu_safe`). ``'lda'`` é a análise discriminante linear do scikit-learn com os seus valores padrão, ``'shrinkage_lda'`` o mesmo com o solver lsqr e encolhimento de Ledoit-Wolf, ``'knn'`` variáveis padronizadas e cinco vizinhos mais próximos, e ``'cpa_<name>'`` um dos classificadores do CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 construído como o CPA o constrói (:func:`spacr.cpa_classifiers.make_cpa_model`). records.context: any of ``"stitch"``, ``"phenotype"``, ``"objects"`` and ``"decode"``, run in that order. A phase left out reads what it needs from the database, so a microplate sample position can be stitched once and decoded again. The alpha phenotype path adds ``"ph_flatfield"``, ``"ph_segment"``, ``"ph_measure"``, ``"ph_masks"``, ``"merge"`` and ``"aggregate"``, run only when named here and after those four; ``ph_flatfield`` builds the laboratory microplate's maps once, before the microplate sample positions, and ``ph_masks`` writes each cell's microscope field of view-edge flags and flat-microscope field of view gains from the saved masks. A processing session of only these needs ``dst_root`` and ``plate`` but no ``genotype_source``, takes its microplate sample positions from ``ops_phenotype``, and adds to each microplate sample position's ``ops_report.json`` rather than replacing it. ``aggregate`` pools the microplate sample positions run and writes ``ops_guides_<plate>`` and ``ops_genes_<plate>``. ``"ph_merged"`` (per microplate sample position, after ``merge``) writes each microscope field of view to ``merged/`` (:func:`_ph_merged`); ``"ph_tables"`` (after ``aggregate``) writes the standard ``measurements/measurements.db`` tables (:func:`_ph_tables`); ``"ph_crops"`` cuts raw extracted image regions of owned cells into a sharded store (:func:`_ph_crops`). ``"ph_ownership"`` (per microplate sample position, after ``ph_masks``) finds the copies of each cell across overlapping microscope fields of view (:func:`_ph_cross_field_ownership`). ``"report"``, last, writes the yield funnel and the counts against a published table to ``results/ops_report/`` (:func:`_ph_report`). With ``ops_ph_secondary_registration`` set, each microplate sample position's second phenotype acquisition is registered before its microscope fields of view are read (:func:`_ph_secondary_shifts`). The alpha ``decode_qc`` phase (items 876 and 877) fits the false-call model and the genotype confidence over the microplate sample positions decoded, writing ``results/ops_decode_qc``; it also executes after ``decode`` when ``ops_decode_qc`` or ``ops_genotype_confidence`` is on. The alpha ``compare_calls`` phase (item 878) matches spaCR's calls to other workflows' per-cell tables (``ops_compare_tables``) and writes ``results/ops_compare``; it also executes after ``decode`` when those tables are set. The alpha profile path, ``"profile"`` and ``"evaluate"``, runs alone: it turns the stored cell tables of ``ops_profile_cells`` into gene profiles and scores them against reference gene pairs (:func:`spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases`); ``"modules"`` builds the module atlas of those profiles (:func:`spacr.ops_modules.run_module_phase`) and ``"mitocarta"`` scores clusterings against MitoCarta and an external module table (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.run_mitocarta_benchmark`); like the profile path, both hold the BLAS and OpenMP pools to one thread while ``ops_deterministic_blas`` is on (the result's ``atlas_blas_threads``). ``"stress"``, after ``report``, times the finished store and writes ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_run_infra.stress_rows`); ``ops_stress_report`` runs it too.
records.label: spacr.ops_engine.run_ops#4
records.source: any of ``"stitch"``, ``"phenotype"``, ``"objects"`` and ``"decode"``, run in that order. A phase left out reads what it needs from the database, so a well can be stitched once and decoded again. The alpha phenotype path adds ``"ph_flatfield"``, ``"ph_segment"``, ``"ph_measure"``, ``"ph_masks"``, ``"merge"`` and ``"aggregate"``, run only when named here and after those four; ``ph_flatfield`` builds the plate's maps once, before the wells, and ``ph_masks`` writes each cell's field-edge flags and flat-field gains from the saved masks. A run of only these needs ``dst_root`` and ``plate`` but no ``genotype_source``, takes its wells from ``ops_phenotype``, and adds to each well's ``ops_report.json`` rather than replacing it. ``aggregate`` pools the wells run and writes ``ops_guides_<plate>`` and ``ops_genes_<plate>``. ``"ph_merged"`` (per well, after ``merge``) writes each field to ``merged/`` (:func:`_ph_merged`); ``"ph_tables"`` (after ``aggregate``) writes the standard ``measurements/measurements.db`` tables (:func:`_ph_tables`); ``"ph_crops"`` cuts raw crops of owned cells into a sharded store (:func:`_ph_crops`). ``"ph_ownership"`` (per well, after ``ph_masks``) finds the copies of each cell across overlapping fields (:func:`_ph_cross_field_ownership`). ``"report"``, last, writes the yield funnel and the counts against a published table to ``results/ops_report/`` (:func:`_ph_report`). With ``ops_ph_secondary_registration`` set, each well's second phenotype acquisition is registered before its fields are read (:func:`_ph_secondary_shifts`). The alpha ``decode_qc`` phase (items 876 and 877) fits the false-call model and the genotype confidence over the wells decoded, writing ``results/ops_decode_qc``; it also runs after ``decode`` when ``ops_decode_qc`` or ``ops_genotype_confidence`` is on. The alpha ``compare_calls`` phase (item 878) matches spaCR's calls to other pipelines' per-cell tables (``ops_compare_tables``) and writes ``results/ops_compare``; it also runs after ``decode`` when those tables are set. The alpha profile path, ``"profile"`` and ``"evaluate"``, runs alone: it turns the stored cell tables of ``ops_profile_cells`` into gene profiles and scores them against reference gene pairs (:func:`spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases`); ``"modules"`` builds the module atlas of those profiles (:func:`spacr.ops_modules.run_module_phase`) and ``"mitocarta"`` scores clusterings against MitoCarta and an external module table (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.run_mitocarta_benchmark`); like the profile path, both hold the BLAS and OpenMP pools to one thread while ``ops_deterministic_blas`` is on (the result's ``atlas_blas_threads``). ``"stress"``, after ``report``, times the finished store and writes ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_run_infra.stress_rows`); ``ops_stress_report`` runs it too.
records.translation: qualquer combinação de ``"stitch"``, ``"phenotype"``, ``"objects"`` e ``"decode"``, executadas nessa ordem. Uma fase deixada de fora lê do banco de dados o que precisa, de modo que um poço pode ser montado uma vez e decodificado de novo. O caminho alfa do fenótipo adiciona ``"ph_flatfield"``, ``"ph_segment"``, ``"ph_measure"``, ``"ph_masks"``, ``"merge"`` e ``"aggregate"``, executadas apenas quando nomeadas aqui e após essas quatro; ``ph_flatfield`` constrói os mapas da placa uma única vez, antes dos poços, e ``ph_masks`` grava os indicadores de borda de campo e os ganhos de campo plano de cada célula a partir das máscaras salvas. Uma execução apenas destas precisa de ``dst_root`` e ``plate`` mas não de ``genotype_source``, obtém os seus poços de ``ops_phenotype`` e acrescenta ao ``ops_report.json`` de cada poço em vez de o substituir. ``aggregate`` agrega os poços executados e grava ``ops_guides_<plate>`` e ``ops_genes_<plate>``. ``"ph_merged"`` (por poço, após ``merge``) grava cada campo em ``merged/`` (:func:`_ph_merged`); ``"ph_tables"`` (após ``aggregate``) grava as tabelas padrão de ``measurements/measurements.db`` (:func:`_ph_tables`); ``"ph_crops"`` corta recortes brutos das células próprias num armazenamento fragmentado (:func:`_ph_crops`). ``"ph_ownership"`` (por poço, após ``ph_masks``) encontra as cópias de cada célula em campos sobrepostos (:func:`_ph_cross_field_ownership`). ``"report"``, por último, grava o funil de rendimento e as contagens frente a uma tabela publicada em ``results/ops_report/`` (:func:`_ph_report`). Com ``ops_ph_secondary_registration`` definido, a segunda aquisição de fenótipo de cada poço é registrada antes de os seus campos serem lidos (:func:`_ph_secondary_shifts`). A fase alfa ``decode_qc`` (itens 876 e 877) ajusta o modelo de chamadas falsas e a confiança do genótipo sobre os poços decodificados, gravando ``results/ops_decode_qc``; também é executada após ``decode`` quando ``ops_decode_qc`` ou ``ops_genotype_confidence`` está ativado. A fase alfa ``compare_calls`` (item 878) associa as chamadas do spaCR às tabelas por célula de outros pipelines (``ops_compare_tables``) e grava ``results/ops_compare``; também é executada após ``decode`` quando essas tabelas estão definidas. O caminho alfa de perfis, ``"profile"`` e ``"evaluate"``, é executado isoladamente: transforma as tabelas de células armazenadas de ``ops_profile_cells`` em perfis de genes e pontua-os frente a pares de genes de referência (:func:`spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases`); ``"modules"`` constrói o atlas de módulos desses perfis (:func:`spacr.ops_modules.run_module_phase`) e ``"mitocarta"`` pontua agrupamentos frente ao MitoCarta e a uma tabela de módulos externa (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.run_mitocarta_benchmark`); tal como o caminho de perfis, ambas mantêm os pools BLAS e OpenMP numa única thread enquanto ``ops_deterministic_blas`` está ativado (o ``atlas_blas_threads`` do resultado). ``"stress"``, após ``report``, cronometra o armazenamento concluído e grava ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_run_infra.stress_rows`); ``ops_stress_report`` também a executa.

records.context: Gene modules of an optical pooled screening experiment: consensus clusters with a known core.
records.label: spacr.ops_modules#0
records.source: Gene modules of an optical pooled screen: consensus clusters with a known core.
records.translation: Módulos de genes de um rastreio óptico agrupado: clusters de consenso com um núcleo conhecido.

records.context: A module is a cluster of the reference clustering that is anchored by known biology (a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway or a GO-slim term enriched in it), together with the genes the screen places next to that core although no resource links them to it. The atlas is built in three steps.
records.label: spacr.ops_modules#1
records.source: A module is a cluster of the reference clustering that is anchored by known biology (a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway or a GO-slim term enriched in it), together with the genes the screen places next to that core although no resource links them to it. The atlas is built in three steps.
records.translation: Um módulo é um cluster do agrupamento de referência ancorado em biologia conhecida (um complexo CORUM, uma via KEGG ou um termo GO-slim enriquecido nele), juntamente com os genes que o rastreio coloca junto desse núcleo embora nenhum recurso os ligue a ele. O atlas é construído em três passos.

records.context: 1. **Partitions.** The gene profiles (targeting genes with more than ten cells, plus the control guides grouped at random into pseudo-genes of four, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) are clustered once with PHATE + Leiden (seed 42) at the resolutions of :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS` (about 70, 250 and 500 clusters), and again ``ops_modules_runs`` times on resampled rows and guides (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`). By default the profiles are standardised and reduced to the components holding 99 % of the variance first. With ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding`` the profile columns are used as they are, which is what a weighted profile (contrastive weighting) needs: standardising it again would undo the weighting. 2. **Anchoring.** In every reference cluster, a one-sided Fisher test for every group of 3 to 500 clustered genes, Benjamini-Hochberg within the cluster; the best group with q < 0.05 and three or more cluster genes is the anchor and its cluster genes are the known core. 3. **Data-selection boundaries.** A gene not linked to the core (no STRING v12 link of 0.4 or more, no BioGRID physical interaction, no shared enriched group) is a stable new member when its co-membership with the core over the consensus runs is above 0.5 and above the 99th percentile of both the control pseudo-genes and 500 fitness-matched random genes, its mean cosine to the core is above that of 1,000 fitness-matched genes (p < 0.01), at least three of its four guides point at the core, and its guides carry no specificity flag.
records.label: spacr.ops_modules#2
records.source: 1. **Partitions.** The gene profiles (targeting genes with more than ten cells, plus the control guides grouped at random into pseudo-genes of four, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) are clustered once with PHATE + Leiden (seed 42) at the resolutions of :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS` (about 70, 250 and 500 clusters), and again ``ops_modules_runs`` times on resampled rows and guides (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`). By default the profiles are standardised and reduced to the components holding 99 % of the variance first. With ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding`` the profile columns are used as they are, which is what a weighted profile (contrastive weighting) needs: standardising it again would undo the weighting. 2. **Anchoring.** In every reference cluster, a one-sided Fisher test for every group of 3 to 500 clustered genes, Benjamini-Hochberg within the cluster; the best group with q < 0.05 and three or more cluster genes is the anchor and its cluster genes are the known core. 3. **Gates.** A gene not linked to the core (no STRING v12 link of 0.4 or more, no BioGRID physical interaction, no shared enriched group) is a stable new member when its co-membership with the core over the consensus runs is above 0.5 and above the 99th percentile of both the control pseudo-genes and 500 fitness-matched random genes, its mean cosine to the core is above that of 1,000 fitness-matched genes (p < 0.01), at least three of its four guides point at the core, and its guides carry no specificity flag.
records.translation: 1. **Partições.** Os perfis de genes (genes-alvo com mais de dez células, mais as guias de controle agrupadas ao acaso em pseudogenes de quatro, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) são agrupados uma vez com PHATE + Leiden (semente 42) nas resoluções de :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS` (cerca de 70, 250 e 500 clusters), e de novo ``ops_modules_runs`` vezes em linhas e guias reamostradas (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`). Por padrão, os perfis são primeiro padronizados e reduzidos às componentes que retêm 99 % da variância. Com ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding``, as colunas de perfil são usadas tal como estão, que é o que um perfil ponderado (ponderação contrastiva) precisa: padronizá-lo de novo desfaria a ponderação. 2. **Ancoragem.** Em cada cluster de referência, um teste de Fisher unilateral para cada grupo de 3 a 500 genes agrupados, Benjamini-Hochberg dentro do cluster; o melhor grupo com q < 0.05 e três ou mais genes do cluster é a âncora e os seus genes do cluster são o núcleo conhecido. 3. **Critérios.** Um gene não ligado ao núcleo (sem ligação STRING v12 de 0.4 ou mais, sem interação física BioGRID, sem grupo enriquecido partilhado) é um novo membro estável quando a sua copertença com o núcleo ao longo das execuções de consenso está acima de 0.5 e acima do percentil 99 tanto dos pseudogenes de controle como de 500 genes aleatórios com fitness correspondente, o seu cosseno médio ao núcleo está acima do de 1,000 genes com fitness correspondente (p < 0.01), pelo menos três das suas quatro guias apontam para o núcleo, e as suas guias não têm nenhum indicador de especificidade.

records.context: Controls: the control pseudo-genes pass through the same data-selection boundaries (empirical FDR), and the gene labels are shuffled three times among the targeting rows and the anchoring and data-selection boundaries recomputed on the same partitions.
records.label: spacr.ops_modules#3

records.context: Cell and cytoplasm rows share ``(prcf, object_label)``; nucleus rows name their cell in ``cell_id``. A cell with several nuclei gets the features of its largest nucleus and ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; nuclei without a cell are not exported. The structured-data names are ``plate``, ``well`` (such as B02), ``site`` and ``Metadata_cell_id``; positions (centroids, bounding boxes, distance to the microscope field of view edge) are kept as ``Location_*`` columns so profile scorers skip them, and bookkeeping columns are dropped, as are the ``pathogen`` distance features a laboratory microplate without a pathogen table carries. Features are ``float32``.
records.label: spacr.screen_staging.export_plate_parquet#1
records.source: Cell and cytoplasm rows share ``(prcf, object_label)``; nucleus rows name their cell in ``cell_id``. A cell with several nuclei gets the features of its largest nucleus and ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; nuclei without a cell are not exported. The keys are ``plate``, ``well`` (such as B02), ``site`` and ``Metadata_cell_id``; positions (centroids, bounding boxes, distance to the field edge) are kept as ``Location_*`` columns so profile scorers skip them, and bookkeeping columns are dropped, as are the ``pathogen`` distance features a plate without a pathogen table carries. Features are ``float32``.
records.translation: As linhas de célula e de citoplasma partilham ``(prcf, object_label)``; as linhas de núcleo nomeiam a sua célula em ``cell_id``. Uma célula com vários núcleos recebe as variáveis do seu maior núcleo e ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; os núcleos sem célula não são exportados. As chaves são ``plate``, ``well`` (como B02), ``site`` e ``Metadata_cell_id``; as posições (centroides, caixas delimitadoras, distância à borda do campo) são mantidas como colunas ``Location_*`` para que os pontuadores de perfis as ignorem, e as colunas de controle interno são descartadas, tal como as variáveis de distância ``pathogen`` que uma placa sem tabela de patógenos traz. As variáveis são ``float32``.

records.context: 1. every microplate sample position gets its laboratory microplate, microplate sample position, compound and concentration (from ``metadata`` when the profiles lack them) and every numeric column outside the structured-data names, counts and ``moa_eval_exclude`` is a feature; 2. each laboratory microplate is normalised to its control microplate sample positions (``moa_eval_normalise``) and a feature without a finite positive scale on some laboratory microplate is dropped; ``moa_eval_feature_qc='standard'`` then drops a feature non-finite in more than 5% of microplate sample positions or above 500 after normalisation (pycytominer's drop_na_columns and drop_outliers, item 807); 3. the labelled microplate sample positions (``moa_eval_labels``, controls left out) are scored by each method of ``moa_eval_methods``, leaving one compound out (:mod:`spacr.moa_benchmark`): ``1nn_cosine`` on treatment profiles (replicate microplate sample positions combined by ``moa_eval_replicates``), and the supervised ``logistic``, ``xgboost``, ``lda``, ``shrinkage_lda``, ``knn`` and the nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 machine-learning classification models ``cpa_<name>`` (:mod:`spacr.cpa_classifiers`) on the microplate sample positions, as ``float32``; 4. per seed the supervised fits use that seed, and the shuffled-label control permutes the compound-to-MoA mapping with generator seed ``seed + 1`` and refits with seeds ``seed + 1 + i`` (the reference's convention at seed 0); the 1-NN control uses generator seed ``seed``. The majority-class control counts the treatments the first method scored.
records.label: spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation#2
records.source: 1. every well gets its plate, well, compound and concentration (from ``metadata`` when the profiles lack them) and every numeric column outside the keys, counts and ``moa_eval_exclude`` is a feature; 2. each plate is normalised to its control wells (``moa_eval_normalise``) and a feature without a finite positive scale on some plate is dropped; ``moa_eval_feature_qc='standard'`` then drops a feature non-finite in more than 5% of wells or above 500 after normalisation (pycytominer's drop_na_columns and drop_outliers, item 807); 3. the labelled wells (``moa_eval_labels``, controls left out) are scored by each method of ``moa_eval_methods``, leaving one compound out (:mod:`spacr.moa_benchmark`): ``1nn_cosine`` on treatment profiles (replicate wells combined by ``moa_eval_replicates``), and the supervised ``logistic``, ``xgboost``, ``lda``, ``shrinkage_lda``, ``knn`` and the nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 classifiers ``cpa_<name>`` (:mod:`spacr.cpa_classifiers`) on the wells, as ``float32``; 4. per seed the supervised fits use that seed, and the shuffled-label control permutes the compound-to-MoA mapping with generator seed ``seed + 1`` and refits with seeds ``seed + 1 + i`` (the reference's convention at seed 0); the 1-NN control uses generator seed ``seed``. The majority-class control counts the treatments the first method scored.
records.translation: 1. cada poço recebe a sua placa, poço, composto e concentração (a partir de ``metadata`` quando os perfis não os têm) e cada coluna numérica fora das chaves, das contagens e de ``moa_eval_exclude`` é uma variável; 2. cada placa é normalizada em relação aos seus poços de controle (``moa_eval_normalise``) e uma variável sem escala positiva finita em alguma placa é descartada; ``moa_eval_feature_qc='standard'`` descarta então uma variável não finita em mais de 5% dos poços ou acima de 500 após a normalização (drop_na_columns e drop_outliers do pycytominer, item 807); 3. os poços rotulados (``moa_eval_labels``, sem os controles) são pontuados por cada método de ``moa_eval_methods``, deixando um composto de fora (:mod:`spacr.moa_benchmark`): ``1nn_cosine`` em perfis de tratamento (poços replicados combinados por ``moa_eval_replicates``), e os supervisionados ``logistic``, ``xgboost``, ``lda``, ``shrinkage_lda``, ``knn`` e os nove classificadores do CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 ``cpa_<name>`` (:mod:`spacr.cpa_classifiers`) nos poços, como ``float32``; 4. em cada semente os ajustes supervisionados usam essa semente, e o controle de rótulos embaralhados permuta o mapeamento composto-MoA com a semente de gerador ``seed + 1`` e reajusta com as sementes ``seed + 1 + i`` (a convenção da referência na semente 0); o controle 1-NN usa a semente de gerador ``seed``. O controle de classe majoritária conta os tratamentos que o primeiro método pontuou.
